incidente.resumo: On January 26 (year not stated), Facebook and Instagram were down for approximately an hour; other sites such as Tinder and HipChat were also affected. Facebook's statements suggested the outage occurred after a change that affected its configuration systems. A third-party analysis (ThousandEyes) saw TCP timeouts and packet loss inside Facebook's network, likely from shutting off traffic, while Instagram returned 503 errors over working TCP connections. TCP connections were allowed again around 11:05pm Pacific, with full service around 11:20pm.

descricao.texto: At 10:10pm Pacific, TCP connections to Facebook timed out, with near complete packet loss seen by the article's monitoring agents; the text does not say how Facebook noticed.
trechos: At 10:10pm Pacific on January 26th, TCP connections to Facebook timed out, as their engineering team likely shut off traffic.
In Figures 3 and 4 you can see the drop in availability caused by TCP connection problems and the near complete packet loss.

descricao.texto: The article quotes Facebook's own post mortem and statements, which suggested the outage occurred after a change was introduced that affected Facebook's configuration systems. The text does not separate a trigger from an underlying defect, and the change itself is not described.
trechos: Facebook’s own post mortem and statements suggested the outage occurred “after we introduced a change that affected our configuration systems."

passos.texto: The analysts infer that Facebook isolated its network to tackle the configuration issues: at 10:10pm Pacific TCP connections timed out as the team likely shut off traffic, with packets dropped at the aggregation switches inside Prineville, likely by an ACL update. Instagram, hosted on AWS, likely did not need the same isolation.
trechos: At 10:10pm Pacific on January 26th, TCP connections to Facebook timed out, as their engineering team likely shut off traffic.
During the outage, packets were dropped within Facebook’s network, likely by an update to their Access Control List (ACL).
Figure 5 shows the path trace with traffic timing out at the aggregation switches inside Prineville, before ever reaching the racks.
This is likely due to the fact that Instagram is hosted on Amazon Web Services and did not require the same sort of network isolation to tackle the configuration issues.

passos.texto: At approximately 11:05pm Facebook began allowing TCP connections again, with full service restored around 11:20pm.
trechos: At approximately 11:05pm, Facebook began allowing TCP connections again, with full service restored around 11:20pm.
For approximately an hour both Facebook and Instagram (owned by Facebook) were completely down

motivo_confianca_baixa: mitigacao: generica or especifica; the only step naming what was acted on (traffic shut off, likely by an ACL update) is the analysts' inference, so the weaker generica was kept.
observacoes: The year is not stated in the text. The text also gives times (10:10pm to 11:20pm, 70 minutes); the stated 'approximately an hour' was used. The ACL update is read as part of the network isolation, as the text links isolation to tackling the configuration issues.
